passage:
A palace garden was restored using old paintings, letters, and plant records. Gardeners tried to recreate paths, ponds, and flower arrangements from the past.
But some plants no longer grew well in the changed climate. The team had to choose similar plants that could survive.
Visitors learned that restoration involves adaptation. A garden is alive, unlike a painting. It changes with weather, soil, insects, and time.
The restored garden was not an exact copy. It was a conversation between history and present conditions.
Living heritage must be cared for as life, not only as design.
